Research question: Deep-dive the ACADEMIC layer of a "ResearchHub" for Epistemos (native macOS research/PKM app, MAS-sandboxed, Swift/URLSession client-side only, optional tiny proxy, keys in Keychain, arXiv ingest already built). A first research pass already covers X/Reddit/HN/GitHub/HF/read-later/RSS + core scholarly APIs (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed, bioRxiv, Crossref, OpenReview) — do NOT re-cover those basics; this pass goes DISCIPLINE-DEEP and COLLEGE-RESOURCE-DEEP. For every source: official API? auth? cost (mid-2026)? rate limits? content licensing/ToS for display? MAS-viable client-side? effort S/M/L? worth-it ranking.

Angle 1 — Journal/publisher access + the paywall problem: Unpaywall API (free OA resolution by DOI), CORE API, DOAJ, OpenAIRE, BASE; publisher APIs and their 2026 terms (Elsevier ScienceDirect/Scopus, Springer Nature, Wiley, IEEE Xplore, ACM DL), PLOS/eLife/Frontiers open APIs, journal RSS/Atom feeds (Nature, Science). How a client app legally shows abstracts/metadata for paywalled papers + one-click OA-copy resolution. Explicitly document what is ILLEGAL to integrate (Sci-Hub, LibGen) so it's excluded by design.

Angle 2 — Discipline-specific indexes and preprint servers: MATH: zbMATH Open API, Project Euclid, MathSciNet (paywalled?), MathOverflow via Stack Exchange API. CS/AI: DBLP API, ACL Anthology, INSPIRE-HEP (physics), Papers With Code post-HF status. BIO/MED: Europe PMC API (free full text!), PubMed Central OA subset, medRxiv. PSYCH/NEURO: PsyArXiv + the OSF preprints API family, APA PsycNet reality, OpenNeuro. CHEM: ChemRxiv. ECON/SOCIAL: SSRN status under Elsevier, RePEc. PHILOSOPHY: PhilPapers API. Which preprint servers share one API (OSF)?

Angle 3 — Google Scholar specifically: confirm the 2026 no-official-API reality, scraping/SerpAPI ToS + cost risk, and the practical substitute stack (OpenAlex + Semantic Scholar + Crossref + Scite?) that replicates Scholar alerts/profiles/citations for a personal app. Can users export their Scholar library/alerts into a file the app imports?

Angle 4 — College/learning resources: MIT OpenCourseWare (feeds/bulk data?), OpenStax + LibreTexts + Open Textbook Library APIs, Khan Academy API status 2026 (retired?), Coursera/edX public catalogs, university open lecture archives (Stanford/Yale OYC) + edu YouTube via RSS or Data API, Internet Archive + Open Library APIs, Project Gutenberg (Gutendex), Wikipedia/Wikidata REST APIs, Stack Exchange network API (Math.SE, CrossValidated, CS.SE), Anki/flashcard ecosystems if API-able.

Angle 5 — Research-graph + discovery infrastructure to power the app's OWN graph view: OpenAlex as backbone (works/authors/citations, free no-auth, polite pool), Semantic Scholar Graph API (citation contexts, TLDRs, recommendations endpoint), CORE, Lens.org, Scite tiers, Connected Papers / ResearchRabbit / Litmaps (public APIs or app-only?), citation-graph edge ingestion patterns for a local knowledge graph, and alert/watch patterns (new-papers-by-author, new-citations-of-paper) implementable client-side.

Deliverable emphasis: per-source verdict table; the "OA resolution chain" recipe (DOI → Unpaywall/OpenAlex → PDF); a discipline coverage map (math/AI/bio/neuro/psych/econ/phil → best 2-3 sources each); Google Scholar substitute verdict; college-resources shortlist; and which sources can feed CITATION EDGES into an existing local graph. 2026-current, official docs preferred, flag 2024-2026 changes.

confirmed.claim: The Unpaywall REST API is free and requires no API key — authentication is just an email query parameter appended to each request, and the live API enforces this by rejecting placeholder emails (a call with an example.com address returns HTTP 422 'Please use your own email address in API calls'). This makes it fully MAS-viable client-side from Swift/URLSession with nothing to store in Keychain.
confirmed.quote: The REST API gives anyone free, programmatic access to the Unpaywall database. [...] Requests must include your email as a parameter at the end of the URL, like this: api.unpaywall.org/my/request?email=YOUR_EMAIL

confirmed.claim: The stated rate limit is 100,000 calls per day (an honor-system 'please limit' request, not a hard enforced quota per the docs), with bulk users directed to snapshot downloads instead — far more than a personal PKM app needs for one-click OA resolution.
confirmed.quote: Please limit use to 100,000 calls per day. If you need faster access, you'll be better served by downloading the entire database snapshot for local access.

confirmed.claim: The GET /v2/:doi endpoint implements the core 'OA resolution chain' step directly: given a DOI it returns OA status plus bibliographic info, and (live-verified 2026-07-03 against 10.1038/nature12373) the JSON includes is_oa, oa_status ('green'), an oa_locations array, and best_oa_location with url_for_pdf (e.g. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1304.1068), url_for_landing_page, license, version, and host_type — i.e., DOI → Unpaywall → legal OA PDF link in one call.
confirmed.quote: Gets OA status and bibliographic info for an given DOI-assigned resource. [...] https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1038/nature12373?email=YOUR_EMAIL

confirmed.claim: Elsevier's free API use cases require the client application itself to be free of charge, non-commercial, and advertising-free — meaning a paid Mac App Store app would not qualify for the free-tier Scopus/SciVal display use cases without a separate commercial agreement.
confirmed.quote: The client application needs to be free of use and non-commercial. This also means that it should be free of advertising.

confirmed.claim: Abstract display rights differ by Elsevier product and use case: ScienceDirect abstracts may be displayed (federated search use case), while Scopus abstracts are explicitly prohibited from public display in the institutional-repository use case and are only permitted for the Academic Research use case.
confirmed.quote: For results from ScienceDirect, the display of abstracts is allowed. ... The following Scopus items may not be displayed publicly: abstracts

confirmed.claim: Elsevier's policy forbids persistently storing or indexing API-retrieved data — only temporary performance caching is allowed — which blocks ingesting Elsevier-sourced metadata/citation edges into a local knowledge graph in perpetuity (with a narrow exception for institutional repositories' own-institution metadata).
confirmed.quote: Data retrieved through the APIs cannot be indexed or stored in a data repository, other than temporarily for performance reasons

confirmed.claim: The IEEE Xplore API license scope is restricted to non-commercial educational, research, or scientific use inside the licensee's own educational institution, so embedding it in a commercially distributed macOS app (like Epistemos on MAS) without a separately negotiated commercial license would violate the terms.
confirmed.quote: non-commercial educational, research, or scientific activities within the Licensee's educational institution

unverified.claim: IEEE's terms forbid bulk retention or bulk presentation of API content — content may only be displayed in response to an individual query — which blocks persisting IEEE metadata/abstracts into a local vault or knowledge graph and blocks feeding IEEE records in as citation edges for offline storage.

IEEE explicitly prohibits using any API content for AI/ML/LLM training, enhancement, or development, a restriction directly relevant to an AI-native PKM app that processes paper metadata with on-device models.

API access is gated to existing IEEE customers (with registration and an API key) unless a specific license is agreed, meaning a general consumer app cannot assume its end users are eligible to obtain keys.

Springer Nature offers a 'Meta API' that exposes metadata and abstracts for millions of its documents — this is the publisher-sanctioned route for a third-party client app (like Epistemos) to display abstracts and metadata for Springer/Nature papers, including paywalled ones, without touching full text.

Springer Nature offers a dedicated 'Open Access API' that returns full-text content of its open-access publications, meaning a DOI→OA-copy resolution chain can terminate at a publisher-direct full-text fetch for SN OA papers rather than relying solely on Unpaywall/OpenAlex.

Full text of Springer Nature's paywalled corpus is only available via the Full Text (TDM) API, which is explicitly scoped to subscription-based content (over 3 million articles across 20+ subject areas) — so client-side full-text access to paywalled SN papers requires a subscription/TDM entitlement and is not viable as a free baseline for a consumer MAS app.

The OpenAIRE Graph API enforces a rate limit of 60 requests per hour for unauthenticated requests and 7,200 requests per hour for authenticated requests, with no payment tier mentioned — making it a free API whose practical ceiling depends only on whether the client registers.

OpenAIRE Graph records are licensed CC-BY and may be re-used commercially in a client app (e.g., displayed in a native macOS PKM) as long as OpenAIRE is credited as the data source — resolving the content-licensing/ToS-for-display question in the app's favor.

The CORE API is free to use without registration at a baseline tier, but organisations that register for faster rates typically pay; Supporting/Sustaining Members get the faster rate free as a member benefit.
CORE's advertised baseline rate limit is one batch request or five single requests per 10 seconds, with faster/VIP rates available only by contacting CORE.

Commercial use of the CORE API is explicitly permitted under CORE's Terms & Conditions, with a 30-day free trial for Institution and Enterprise tiers and an eligibility assessment for free licences during registration — relevant because a Mac App Store app is a commercial integration.
The CORE API provides real-time machine access to full texts of open-access research papers, not just metadata, making it usable as a full-text retrieval node in a DOI-to-PDF OA resolution chain.

OSF APIv2 permits anonymous (unauthenticated) read access but caps it at 100 requests/hour, while authenticated requests get 10,000/day; 429 responses carry a Retry-After header. This makes a Keychain-stored personal token effectively required for any serious client-side preprint polling in Epistemos.

Authentication is a user-created Personal Access Token sent as a Bearer header (created at osf.io/settings/tokens, with limitable scopes) or an OAuth 2.0 web-application flow — plain HTTPS REST with no SDK requirement, so it is MAS-viable via URLSession with the token in Keychain.

One API serves all OSF-hosted preprint servers: the /v2/preprints/ endpoint filters by provider (the spec names OSF, socarxiv, and psyarxiv as example providers), and provider-scoped endpoints exist at /providers/preprints/{provider_id}/preprints/ plus per-provider taxonomies, licenses, and subjects — confirming PsyArXiv-family servers share the single OSF API. Filtering on date_created/date_modified enables client-side new-preprint alert polling.
Europe PMC provides an official REST API operated by EMBL-EBI (with the Europe PMC Funders' Group and NLM), making it a first-party institutional source rather than a scraper or third-party wrapper.

The API exposes large-scale free full-text and open-access content (10.2M full-text articles, 6.5M OA articles across 33M+ publications), directly supporting the 'Europe PMC = free full text' claim for the BIO/MED discipline lane.
The API provides citation-network and reference-list data (reference lists for 19.4M+ publications plus citation counts), which can feed citation EDGES into the app's local knowledge graph.
